corpus_item: RI-QST01, RI-QST02 (D1/D3/D4/D5/D6/D8/D9), RI-QST03, RI-CRM02 §1-§4 (the Warrant of Attainder)
note: The Imperial Assize, rank 0 to rank 7. The civil arm of the Provincial Office at Gideon:
customs, the toll book, and the only courts in the province (RI-LOR02 §3, §4.5).
The line's subject is the Blackrose labour-lease — 'prisoners rented out to coastal
plantations and, through intermediaries, to Dres factors. Legal on paper. Slavery in fact'
(RI-LOR02 §3). The corruption reveal lands at rank 2, and the reveal is not that somebody is
corrupt. It is that nobody is: the lease is lawful, audited, and audited by the office that
writes it, and the player has been the paperwork since rank 0.
RI-CRM02 §2 is implemented as content at rank 5: a Warrant of Attainder is lawful inside
Imperial jurisdiction and void everywhere else, does not suppress witnesses, does not cover
collateral, and is recalled after fourteen days with the target told your name. Three of the
four resolutions on that quest do not end in a corpse, which is RI-CRM02 §3's requirement
that no writ execution be built as an encounter that can only end in one.

quests.title: Two Copies of the Same Morning

giver.location: Gideon, the court room behind the Provincial compound

quests.directions: The court is the long room behind the Provincial compound at Gideon, past the yard where the carts stand. The fair copy goes up to the Governor's clerk on the compound's first floor and the day-book stays with the notary, and the two are never carried by the same person because of a rule nobody at the court can now explain.

journal.text: The customs clerk at Soulrest said the Assize is always short a hand in Second Seed and that a pair of hands that can carry paper without reading it will do.

Assizer Corvo has put me on the morning carry. The fair copy goes up to the Governor's clerk, the day-book stays below, and I am not to let them travel together. He said it as a rule, not as a caution.
I have carried the pair for six mornings. On four of them the two documents differ by exactly one entry and the entry is always a lease chit out of Blackrose.
The rule about not carrying them together is not a rule. It is a habit that started with a notary who was struck off eleven years ago and it has outlived everyone who knew why.

I let the fair copy and the day-book travel in the same hand on a wet morning and both of them went into the yard puddle. Corvo has put me on the door instead. He was decent about it and he has not asked me back.
Six mornings, both books, no remarks. Corvo has written me onto the roll as a clerk of the Assize, which he says is the least anyone has ever been given for the most anyone has ever noticed.

I copied the four differing entries onto the back of a customs form before I handed either book over. Corvo has put me on the roll and does not know I am carrying a seventh document up the stairs every morning.

branches.condition: The player has noticed the two books differ and has a morning alone with both

resolutions.outcome: The player is on the roll of the Assize and has noticed something they cannot yet name. The office notices nothing at all, which is the office working correctly.

The player is on the roll and holds four transcribed lease chits nobody knows exist. Every quest in this line for the next four ranks is easier because of it and one of them is only reachable because of it.

failure_states.cause: The player carries both books in one trip
failure_states.consequence: The player is moved to the door and the line closes at rank 0. Corvo will still speak to them and will not put them back on the carry.

rewards.name: the court room behind the Provincial compound

quests.notes: Rank 0. RI-QST01: errands establish texture and geography. The texture here is that the Assize is a filing system, and the whole line's corruption is visible on the first morning as a one-entry discrepancy nobody has ever been paid to look at.
quests.joins_note: Every ending of the entry quest ends with the player taken on — on the roll, named by the hollow, sent again. That is the JOIN, and it is authored here rather than derived, because mutual exclusion now keys on membership: reputation paid sideways by another faction's quest is a qualification, not a career (see game/src/sim/quest/machine.js heldRank).

quests.title: Forty Years of River

giver.location: Tidewrack, the survey hut above the landing

quests.directions: Doren keeps the survey hut above the Tidewrack landing and works with the shutters open in any weather. The old toll volumes are in the Gideon court's under-room, behind the door the yard cats use, and they are stacked by season and not by year, which is the whole difficulty.

journal.text: Clerk Doren wants the toll volumes for the four seasons before the Governor arrived. She is compiling a return for Cyrodiil and says the compilation is a formality. She said formality twice.
The under-room holds forty years of river in no order at all. Three of the four volumes I need are where they should be. The fourth is not in the room and the yard cats have not eaten it.

The missing volume was signed out eleven years ago by a notary called Sedda Vell and never signed back in, and the sign-out book is the only place in the Assize where her name has not been struck through.
Vell drinks at the Blackrose inn and has the volume. She says she took it because it was going to be corrected and she wanted a copy of what it said before it was made to say something else.
Doren's return went to Cyrodiil with three volumes and a note saying the fourth was lost in the flood of the year before last. There was no flood the year before last.
Four volumes on Doren's table. She looked at the fourth for a long time before she opened it and then she did not say anything about where it had been.

Vell gave me the volume on condition I read the Archon entries first, standing there, in front of her. I read them. Forty years of river and every one of the Dres hulls is in the fourth volume and none of them is in the other three.
I left the volume with Vell and told Doren it was gone. She wrote lost, which is a word the office accepts, and then she asked me who had it, and I did not answer, and she did not ask again.

branches.condition: The player has found the struck-off notary and she is holding the volume

resolutions.outcome: The volume returns to the under-room and the return goes to Cyrodiil complete. Nothing in it is read by anyone who did not already know what it said.
The player reads forty years of Archon in one sitting and then hands the book in. The office gets its volume. The player gets the shape of the thing the office is for.

The volume stays out of the office and the office writes the word it uses for that. Doren knows the player lied and files it anyway, which tells the player more about the Assize than the book would have.

failure_states.cause: The Cyrodiil packet leaves Gideon before the player reaches the Blackrose inn
failure_states.consequence: The return goes short and is recorded as a flood loss. The volume stays with Vell and rank 2 opens without the player having met her.

deceit.stated_objective: Fetch four toll volumes for a routine return to Cyrodiil
deceit.actual_objective: The same thing, honestly asked. What is not honest is the office's habit of correcting a volume before it is read
deceit.truth: The fourth volume is the only one that records the Dres hulls at Archon, and it was signed out eleven years ago by the notary the office struck off.

quests.notes: Rank 1. The dissenter arrives here rather than at rank 4, because the Assize's rot is a filing habit rather than a person and it needs somebody to point at it early. Vell's reveal is cited by two of the three resolutions' requires_knowing, so she unlocks branches rather than merely having opinions (RI-QST02 D3's test).

quests.title: Lawful, Audited, and Audited by Us

giver.location: Gideon, the court room behind the Provincial compound

quests.directions: Corvo will hand it over in the court room and will not walk you out. The lease roll is kept at Blackrose, in the Prefect's outer office, and the road inland from Gideon goes by the Chelnisi ford and then two days of drained ground with nothing on it but the lease gangs.

journal.text: Corvo wants the Blackrose lease roll reconciled against the customs returns. He says it is an audit and that the Assize does one every four years. He did not say what the last three found.
The roll is exact. Six hundred and eleven leased out this season, six hundred and eleven returned, signed at both ends. The signature at both ends is the same hand.

The plantations that take the leases are four, and two of them buy their salt from a factor at Archon, and the factor at Archon is House Dres. Nothing in that sentence is unlawful anywhere in the Empire.

Sedda Vell says the audit has been done three times and has come back exact three times, because the audit reconciles the roll against the returns and both of those are written at Blackrose. She has the day-books that are not.

I have read what a lease looks like from underneath. A man goes out on a chit for a season and the season is renewed by the office that wrote the chit, and there is no number anywhere for how many seasons a man may be renewed.
The roll was sent up to Gideon before I got to it, by a courier the Prefect's office says it did not send. Corvo has the reconciliation already and it is exact.

I filed it exact, because it is exact. Corvo signed it without reading past the first line. The Assize has audited the labour-lease for the fourth time in sixteen years and found nothing wrong with it, and I am the reason for the fourth.

I filed it exact and wrote a second finding underneath about the renewal clause. Corvo read that one twice, put it in a drawer, and told me the drawer was the correct place for it and that he meant that.

I took the reconciliation to Vell instead and she matched it against eleven years of her own day-books in one evening. Two hundred and nine men have been renewed past four seasons. None of them is in any roll the Assize has ever audited.

branches.condition: The player has the roll, the returns, and has noticed both are written at Blackrose

resolutions.outcome: The audit clears. The lease continues. The player is now, in the only sense the record cares about, the person who checked.

The renewal clause is written down inside the Assize, where it can be found later by somebody who goes looking. Corvo files it in the drawer and tells the player he means it, which is the most honest thing anyone in this office says to them.
Two hundred and nine names come out of a struck-off notary's day-books and into the player's hands. The Assize's audit still clears, because nobody told the Assize.

failure_states.cause: Twelve days pass after journal index 10 without the player reaching the Prefect's outer office
failure_states.consequence: Somebody reconciles it first. Only res_file_exact remains and the player signs a finding they did not make.

deceit.stated_objective: Reconcile the Blackrose lease roll against the customs returns
deceit.actual_objective: Produce a fourth clean audit, by a route that has produced three, so that the lease has been checked again
deceit.truth: The roll and the returns are both written at Blackrose in the same hand, so the audit cannot find anything, and the renewal clause has no upper number in it.

rewards.name: a list of two hundred and nine names

quests.notes: Rank 2 and the corruption reveal, inside RI-QST01's hard deadline of rank 3. The reveal is structural rather than personal: the audit is honest, the auditor is honest, the lease is lawful, and six hundred and eleven people are property. That is the Morrowind Imperial Legion shape (D4's Vabdas order) at institutional scale.

quests.title: The Widow at the Chelnisi Ford

giver.location: Tidewrack, the survey hut above the landing

quests.directions: Doren will give you the writ at the survey hut. The holding is at the Chelnisi ford where the Gideon road crosses, a reed-house and a fish weir on the near bank, and the widow keeps it alone since the survey works took her husband under.

journal.text: Doren has given me a writ of possession for a holding at the Chelnisi ford. The survey needs the bank for the new cut. She says the compensation was offered and refused and that the refusal is on file.
The widow is called Ineel-Sa and her husband drowned in the survey's own trial cut two winters ago. The compensation on file was offered to him, by name, four months after he died.

She will not take money and she will not leave and she has said both to four people before me. She is not being difficult. The weir is the only reason her hatchlings eat and there is no other bank on that reach.

Vell says the cut can go on the far bank for about a third more and that the survey knows it, and that the near bank was chosen because the near bank had a holding on it that the office expected to fold.

The writ was executed by the militia while I was still arguing about it in Gideon. The reed-house is down, the weir is cut, and Ineel-Sa is somewhere on the Gideon road with three hatchlings and a compensation chit made out to a dead man.

I served the writ. She read it, which I had not expected, and then she put her mark on it and asked me to carry the chit back because it has her husband's name on it and she does not want it in the house.

I took the survey the far-bank figures and made them argue against a third more cost with two hundred and nine names sitting on the table. The cut goes on the far bank. It cost the Assize four hundred and it cost me Doren.

I returned the writ unserved and wrote the reason on the back of it. Corvo has entered the refusal on the roll against my name, which is what a refusal is for, and the writ has gone to another server.

I bought the holding off her at four times the compensation, out of my own purse, and served the writ on myself. Every party got what the file says they wanted. She is on the Gideon road with money instead of nothing, which is not the same as being right.

branches.condition: The player has met the widow and read the compensation date

resolutions.outcome: The writ is served lawfully and the holding comes down. It is the correct execution of a lawful instrument and it is the worst thing in this line the player does with a clear conscience available to them.

The cut moves to the far bank at a third more cost, argued through on figures rather than on mercy. The holding stands. Doren does not speak to the player again and the office notes that they can be argued into things.

The writ comes back with a reason written on it. The refusal goes on the roll against the player's name, which costs standing and buys a record that somebody objected. Somebody else serves it within the month.

The player pays four times the compensation out of their own purse and executes the writ against themselves. The file is satisfied, the survey is satisfied, and a family is on the road with money — which the office will record as a success and the player will not.

failure_states.cause: Nine days pass after journal index 24 without the player resolving the writ
failure_states.consequence: The militia executes it. `assize_seal_held` is not raised, so rank 5 never opens for a player who let it happen by delay rather than by decision.

deceit.stated_objective: Serve a lawful writ of possession on a holding whose compensation was offered and refused
deceit.actual_objective: Clear the near bank cheaply, having chosen it because the holding on it was expected to fold
deceit.truth: The compensation was offered to a man four months after the survey's own trial cut drowned him, and the far bank would work for about a third more.

rewards.name: the holding at the Chelnisi ford

quests.notes: Rank 3. RI-QST02 D4 is the whole quest — Morrowind's Vabdas order, reconstructed: a lawful instrument from a legitimate authority that is unjust on inspection, with refusal implemented as a first-class resolution that has an outcome, a cost, and is not a failure state. Three of the four resolutions raise `assize_seal_held`, which is the rank-5 world state; res_return_unserved does not, so the player who refuses pays for it at the ladder as well as at the roll.

quests.title: Two Hundred and Nine
quests.directions: Hallow keeps the outer office at Blackrose and signs at a standing desk. The day-books are in a room at the inn where Vell lodges, in a chest she sits on, and the inn is the second building past the fortress gate on the yard side.

journal.text: Prefect Hallow wants a set of old day-books recovered from a former officer of the court. He calls them the property of the Assize. He has said the word property four times and has not once said her name.
The office has never asked for them back in eleven years, because asking would concede they exist. Hallow is asking now, which means something has changed and it has not changed at Blackrose.
The lease vote is in Second Seed. Four seats. If the day-books reach the vote the lease falls and four careers fall with it, and one of the four is a Prefect who signs at a standing desk.
Vell will give them up. Not to the office — to the vote. She says she has waited eleven years to be asked by a person who was going to do something and she is not certain I am, and neither am I.

The yard hands at Blackrose know exactly who the two hundred and nine are. They have been counting them for six seasons in a way that leaves no paper. They will say the names aloud to a stranger and they will not write one down.
The inn burned in the night, which inns do. Vell is alive and has nothing, and she will not speak to me, and I cannot prove to her that it was not me.
I took the day-books and gave them to Hallow. He did not open them in front of me. The lease vote is in Second Seed and there is now nothing on the table but the roll, and the roll is exact.

I carried the day-books to Gideon and lodged them with the court against the vote. Hallow has written to the Legate about me. Vell walked to Gideon behind me the whole way and did not once ask to carry them.

I copied the two hundred and nine, gave Hallow the books, and kept the copy. He is satisfied, Vell is not, and I have the only surviving list and the only person who knows I have it is a man in a yard who cannot write.

I told Hallow the books had burned before I got there and I told Vell to move. She is at Soulrest under an undertaker's roof, which is the one place in this province that does not get searched, and the vote goes ahead with nothing on the table.

branches.condition: The player knows the vote is in Second Seed and that the day-books decide it

resolutions.outcome: Eleven years of day-books go into the Prefect's office and are not seen again. The lease vote will have the roll and nothing else. The player is trusted absolutely by four people who are now permanently in their debt.

The day-books are lodged with the court against the vote, in the open, by an officer of the Assize acting within their own authority. It is entirely lawful and it makes an enemy of a Prefect and a friend of nobody who can help.

failure_states.consequence: The day-books burn and the dissenter stops speaking to the player for the rest of the line. The lease vote goes ahead with the roll and nothing else.

rewards.name: a list of two hundred and nine names

quests.notes: Rank 4, first of two. RI-QST02 D8: two of the four resolutions permanently lock Q-XULA-04 and the Deep-Kin line with it, and the journal says so in first person on the day it happens rather than in a modal. The X3 escape is res_lodge_them and res_hide_vell, both gated on the dissenter's own terms.

quests.title: A Warrant That Does Not Travel
quests.directions: Arn holds the writ-room in the Stormhold garrison, up the stair from the stores depot in the walled quarter. The warrant names a Dres factor at Archon and Archon is chartered, so the warrant is good there; the man himself keeps a house at Thorn, and Thorn is not.

journal.text: Prefect Arn has issued me a Warrant of Attainder against a Dres salt-factor called Neloth Vaun. It is lawful inside Imperial ground, void everywhere else, and it comes back to the office in fourteen days whether or not it has been used.

It clears the bounty on the name written on it. It clears nothing else. Not the door, not the man who steps in the way, not the witnesses, who still see me and still report and whose report simply resolves the other way.

Vaun keeps his household at Thorn, which is not Imperial ground and has no bounty at all, and comes down to Archon for the water-calls. Getting him onto chartered ground is the work. The other part is not the part that goes wrong.

I have talked to him. He has a version of it. He says the Empire has attainted him for moving what the Empire's own toll book records and taxes, and he offered to show me his receipts, and then he showed me his receipts.
He will pay four thousand to be left alone, and he will pay it at Thorn where nothing I do about it is lawful. He has made this offer before and the office has never asked whether anyone took it.
Fourteen days. The warrant is recalled and the office has told Vaun who was carrying it, which is what the office does, and there is a man at Thorn who now knows my name and what it was for.

It was done at Archon on chartered ground with the warrant in my hand. Four witnesses, four reports, and all four resolved lawful. The Cohort took the body. The bill for the doorman was sixteen hundred and the warrant did not touch it.

I put him on a hull out of Archon with his household and his receipts and returned the warrant marked absent. Arn accepted it at half the fee and wrote the word departed, which is a word the office is comfortable with.

I laid his own receipts before the Assize instead. He is not dead and he is not attainted; he is ruined, publicly, in the toll book he was so proud of being in. Arn says the office wanted a result and this is one.
I gave the warrant back unserved. Arn took two ranks of progress off me for it and told me the office would send another, and it has, and I expect I will hear about it.

branches.condition: The player holds the warrant, knows where the target lives and knows where the warrant is good

resolutions.outcome: A lawful killing on chartered ground, four lawful reports, and a bill for everything the warrant did not cover. The office is entirely satisfied and the player has learned what a writ is worth, which is exactly the name written on it.

The target and his household leave the province on a hull he paid for. The warrant is returned marked absent and the office pays half. Archon loses its factor and House Dres sends another within the year.

RI-CRM02 §2 and §3 as playable content: the warrant is jurisdictional, does not suppress witnesses, does not cover collateral, expires in fourteen days and tells the target your name when it does. Three of four resolutions are non-lethal, and D6 is satisfied — the target talks, has receipts, and one resolution is only reachable through what he says.

quests.title: The Prefect's Return

giver.location: Gideon, the court room behind the Provincial compound

quests.directions: Corvo has stopped meeting in the court room and takes this one in the yard where the carts stand. The vote sits on the counting floor of the Provincial compound in Second Seed and the four seats come up from Blackrose, Lilmoth, Soulrest and the compound's own first floor.

journal.text: Corvo has told me what he has been carrying for six seasons. The Prefect's return that certifies the lease is sound has been copied out in a Gideon hand every year, and the Gideon hand is his.

He did it the first year because the return was late and the packet was leaving. He did it the sixth year because he had done it five times. He is not asking me to forgive that. He is asking me to decide what happens in Second Seed.

Four seats. Doren votes with the survey. Hallow votes for the lease. The Governor's clerk votes with whoever wrote the paper in front of him. Corvo has one vote and has decided to abstain, and told me so before I asked.

If the lease falls, six hundred and eleven people walk out of Blackrose into a province with no work in it. Vell has thought about that for eleven years and has no answer either. She says having no answer is not a reason to keep the lease.
Second Seed came and went while I was on the coast. The lease stands, the return was signed at Blackrose for once, and Corvo has taken a posting at Stormhold.

The lease stands. I argued it standing, on the six hundred and eleven who would have nowhere to go, and I believe about half of what I said. Hallow shook my hand. That is the part I keep coming back to.

The lease fell. Two hundred and nine renewals read into the record, the day-books on the table, and Corvo's own six returns read out by Corvo. Blackrose empties in a season and not a person in that room could say where to.

The lease stands with a term on it. Four seasons, no renewal, audited from Gideon by a clerk who has never been to Blackrose. It is a worse answer than ending it and a better one than the last sixteen years, and it is mine.

branches.condition: The player has the seats counted and knows what the giver has been signing

resolutions.outcome: The labour-lease is confirmed for another four years by an Assize that has now examined it properly and kept it anyway. That is a worse thing than never having looked, and the player did it with their eyes open.
resolutions.requires_note: Lowered under the MEASURED ceiling for this attribute (reports/faction-signature-sweep.json: base + 6 per governing skill, character/derive.js:359). At the old figure this quest had NO reachable ending for a p10 signature and the questline dead-ended on its own last rank. tools/quests/resolution-reachability.mjs is the check.

resolutions.outcome: The lease ends. Six hundred and eleven people are free and destitute in the same afternoon, four careers end, and the province gains a labour problem it has no institution capable of holding. It is the right answer and it is not a happy one.

quests.title: Whatever Blackrose Is Now

giver.location: Stormhold, the archive under the garrison

quests.directions: Hulen works in the archive under the Stormhold garrison, past the stores in the walled quarter, and does not come up. Blackrose is four days inland from Gideon by the drained road and the Prefect's office is inside the second gate, and after the vote there is a great deal less between the gates than there was.

journal.text: Scribe Hulen has written to me from the Stormhold archive. The Prefect of Blackrose has not filed a return since the vote and the archive is required to have one. He calls it a filing matter.

Hallow has not filed because there is nothing to file. The fortress is holding six hundred and eleven people it can no longer lease and cannot feed, or it is holding a hundred and sixty it could not release, depending on which way Second Seed went.
Hulen does not want a return. He wants Hallow removed and a return filed by whoever replaces him, and he has picked me because I am the only officer of the Assize who has been inside Blackrose twice.
Hallow has been at Blackrose eleven years and has asked for a transfer nine times. The nine requests are in the archive Hulen works in. Hulen has read them.
Vell says Hallow is not the lease. He is the man they put in front of it, and if he goes another one arrives in a season and the archive gets its return and nothing else changes at all.
Hallow filed. It arrived at Stormhold a day before I did, four pages, correct in every particular and signed at Blackrose. Hulen has thanked me for my trouble.
I laid the nine transfer requests and the unfiled return before the Legate and Hallow was relieved within the day. The Prefect's chair at Blackrose is empty and Hulen has his filing.
I filed the return for him, out of what I had seen with my own eyes, and signed it as an officer of the Assize. Hallow keeps the chair. Hulen has stopped writing to me and the Legate has started.

I took Hallow's ninth transfer request to the Legate as a resignation and he did not deny it. He is out of the province by the first packet and the chair is empty and he thanked me for it, which I did not expect and did not enjoy.
I told Hulen that the archive could want its return from another hand. He has written to the Legate about me. Hallow is still at Blackrose with whatever Blackrose is now, and so is everyone in it.

branches.condition: The player knows the giver wants a removal rather than a return

resolutions.outcome: Hallow is relieved on the strength of nine requests to be relieved. The chair is empty, the archive is satisfied, and the man who ran the lease for eleven years is punished for wanting to stop.

The return is filed by the player, out of what they saw, and the chair stays occupied. The archive is satisfied by a document rather than by a removal, and the Legate now knows the player's name for the wrong reason.

quests.notes: Rank 6, and the quest that vacates the seat rank 7 requires. RI-QST02 D11: the man who has run the labour-lease for eleven years is given the coherent account in which he is the reasonable party, in dialogue, at length, and the player can press on it. Not one of the four resolutions is combat.

quests.title: The Legate's Seal

giver.location: Gideon, the Legate's room on the compound's first floor

quests.directions: The Legate's room is on the compound's first floor at Gideon, at the end of the corridor the carry goes up every morning. The seal is in the second drawer and the drawer has never been locked, because in nineteen years nobody has been mad enough to take it.

journal.text: The Legate has gone home on the winter packet and the Elder Council has not sent another. Corvo says the province has an Assize with an empty chair at the head of it and a seal in an unlocked drawer, and that he is telling me because I am next on the roll.
The seal closes a finding for good. Anything sealed cannot be reopened in this province and can only be reopened in Cyrodiil, and Cyrodiil is two letters a year and has never once written back.

There are four findings open. The lease, the Archon toll book, the two hundred and nine renewals, and the Ledger's eighth chair. Every one of them can be closed or opened by the same piece of brass in the same afternoon.

Vell says the seal was made to stop a governor reopening a case out of spite, and that it has been used forty times and thirty-nine of those were to stop a case being opened at all. She would like it back on a boat to Cyrodiil.
The Elder Council sent a Legate after all, on the spring packet, a Colovian with instructions and no interest in the province. The four findings are his now. I am a Prefect.

I took the seal and closed all four. The lease, the toll book, the renewals, the eighth chair, sealed in one afternoon alone in a room with the door shut. The province is quiet. I have never been so certain that quiet is a thing that is done to people.

I took the seal and opened all four instead, and sealed the openings so no successor can shut them. Four findings running in a province with one court and no Legate, and I have made a great many powerful people's next four years my problem.

I sealed the two hundred and nine and left the other three open. Those men are free and unappealable. The lease, the toll book and the eighth chair go on being arguments, which is what they should be, and I have used the brass once.

I put the seal on the packet to Cyrodiil with a letter under it saying what it had been used for forty times. The Assize is a court with no way to close anything. Corvo says it will not survive the year. He may be right and I would do it again.

branches.condition: The player is Legate in fact, alone in the room, with four open findings and the drawer

resolutions.outcome: Everything is closed and cannot be reopened. The Assize becomes what it was always tending toward: an instrument for making questions stop. The player is the institution, and the institution is the drawer.
All four findings are opened and the openings sealed, so no successor can shut them. The province gets four years of court and the player gets four years of everyone who matters wanting them gone.

failure_states.cause: The spring packet reaches Gideon before the player takes the seal
failure_states.consequence: A Legate arrives from Cyrodiil and the four findings are his. The line ends at Prefect and the province's four open questions are decided by somebody the player never meets.

deceit.stated_objective: Hold the Assize until the Elder Council sends a Legate
deceit.actual_objective: The same, honestly offered. The lie in this quest is not the giver's — it is the office's account of what the seal is for
deceit.truth: The seal was made so a governor could not reopen a case to punish somebody. It has been used forty times and thirty-nine of those were to stop a case being opened at all.

rewards.name: a verbal account accepted at any Imperial arrest

quests.notes: Rank 7. Succession by vacancy rather than by removal, which is the Imperial version: nobody is killed, the Elder Council simply does not send anyone. All four resolutions are non-violent and the line's whole argument — that a lawful institution with nobody watching it is more dangerous than a corrupt one — is decided in a single afternoon with a piece of brass. `acc_assize_verbal_account` is RI-CRM02 §6's Cohort-rank-4 dismissal, granted here as the terminal reward.

quests.title: The Oath Nobody Reads

giver.location: Gideon, the Assize court on the upper floor

quests.directions: Doren works the outer desk under the window and the oath book is chained to the lectern beside the door, which is the only thing in the building that is chained to anything.

journal.text: Doren wants four oaths witnessed before the court sits. Three of the four are for men who have been in the Assize's service since before she was born.
Nobody reads the oath. Each of them put a hand on the book, said the last four words with the clerk, and signed, and the whole thing took less time than the walk to the lectern.
The fourth is a bargeman from Soulrest who has never sworn anything in his life. He read it. He read all of it, twice, and then asked me what a distraint is.
The oath binds the swearer to report any officer of the court who takes a fee outside the roll. Three men signed that this morning without looking at it and one man read it and went pale.
The court sat with three oaths on the roll instead of four, and the bargeman is on the water going home, and nobody in the building asked why.
Four oaths, witnessed, on the roll. I told the bargeman what a distraint is and I watched him decide to sign anyway, which is not the same as not knowing.
Three oaths. I told the bargeman what the fourth clause would cost a man who works a river for a living, and he thanked me and did not sign.

resolutions.outcome: Four names on the roll and one of them belongs to a man who now knows what he signed.
The roll is short by one and the Assize learns what kind of witness it has hired.

failure_states.cause: The court sits before the fourth oath is witnessed
failure_states.consequence: The oath waits a season and Doren does the next one herself.

quests.title: A Seal in the Wrong Wax

giver.location: Gideon, the Assize court on the upper floor

quests.directions: Corvo keeps the impressions in the drawer under the bench, and the distraint that carries the wrong wax is filed at the gate house in Gideon with the season's tolls.

journal.text: Corvo wants a distraint order back off the gate house before the season closes, and he described it by its wax rather than by its number, which is a strange way to describe a document.
Assize wax is grey and comes from one supplier under contract. This one is grey and it is not that grey, and Corvo saw the difference across a room.
The seal is right. The impression is the Legate's own and the die that made it has been in the same drawer for nine years. It is the wax that is wrong and the wax is the part nobody guards.
Vell was struck off for exactly this and has been saying for two years that the die leaves the building. Everybody has been arguing about the die.
The season closed with the distraint still on file and the gate house has sent the whole season's papers up to Blackrose in one crate, where they will be read in four years or never.
The order is back in the drawer and Corvo put it in the fire in front of me without reading it, which tells me he already knew what it said.
The order is back and it is on the bench, entered, numbered and impossible to lose. Corvo has not spoken to me since and the wax question is now a matter of record.
Vell has it. She has been right for two years about the wrong thing and now she has the right thing in her hand, and she has not decided yet what that is worth.

deceit.stated_objective: Recover a distraint order sealed in the wrong wax before the season closes
deceit.actual_objective: Get the only physical proof that Assize seals are being struck outside the building off the file before it is crated to Blackrose
deceit.truth: The die never left the drawer. Somebody in the building is striking real seals into wax they bought themselves, and the wax is the only thing that shows it.

resolutions.outcome: The evidence comes home and goes in the fire, and the player watched it happen.
Entered and numbered, which makes it a thing the court has to answer for.
The struck-off notary gets the proof and the court gets a problem it cannot burn.

failure_states.cause: The season's gate-house papers are crated for Blackrose
failure_states.consequence: The order goes into a crate and the question waits four years.

quests.title: The Room With No Case In It

giver.location: Gideon, the yard behind the court

quests.directions: The door is on the half-landing between the record floor and the court, painted the same grey as the wall, and the key hangs on the same ring as every other key in the building.

journal.text: There is a room on the half-landing that is on no plan of this building and is not locked. It has a table, two chairs and a window that has been bricked from the outside.
Nothing in the room is a record. There are eleven chairs' worth of wear on a floor that has two chairs on it, and the wear is in a circle.
The bricking is from outside and the mortar is Imperial and old. Somebody bricked a window on a room they meant to keep using, which is the opposite of abandoning it.
Vell says the room is where the province was governed for eleven years while the Legate was in Cyrodiil, and that no minute of any meeting in it exists because that was the point of the room.
She also says the last meeting in it was four years ago and that Hallow was in the circle, and she says it without any evidence at all, which is what got her struck off.
The half-landing door has a lock on it now, new, and the key is not on the ring. I looked at a room for three days and the building looked back.

The room is on the plan now. I filed a note of its existence, its dimensions and its eleven chairs, and the note is numbered, and a numbered note is the one thing in this province that does not go away.
The table and the chairs are in the record floor and the room is a cupboard for lamp oil. It will be a room again the week after anybody stops looking.
I said nothing and put the key back on the ring. It is the only room in this building I know the shape of and nobody knows I know it.

resolutions.outcome: The room becomes a fact in the record, which is the only permanence this court has.
A gesture with a shelf life, and the journal knows it.
The player keeps a room nobody else admits exists, which two later quests read.

failure_states.cause: The player is seen on the half-landing three times
failure_states.consequence: A lock appears, the key leaves the ring, and the room goes back to not existing.

quests.title: Eleven Years of Not Asking
quests.directions: Hallow will see anybody in the return room at Blackrose between the two bells, and the eleven years of returns she wants read are in the long press against the damp wall where the bottom four are stuck together.

journal.text: Hallow wants eleven years of prefect's returns read and summarised, and she wants the summary in one page, and she said the number eleven three times.
Eleven years is exactly how long since the last Legate left the province. The returns before that are in a different press and are in better order.
Every return in eleven years has been signed by a prefect and countersigned by nobody, because there has been nobody in the province entitled to countersign one.
The bottom four are stuck together with damp and they are the four that cover the labour-lease. Damp is a very convenient reader.

Separated with a knife and a kettle, the four say what the other seven do not: the lease was renewed by a prefect who wrote in his own return that he had no authority to renew it, and then renewed it.
Hallow was that prefect's clerk. She has known where the damp is for eleven years and she has just sent somebody who does not know her to go and find it.
The long press was cleared for the season's move to Gideon and the eleven years are in a barge hold under the tolls, which is where documents in this province go to be safe from being read.
One page, eleven years, no mention of the four that were stuck. Hallow read it in front of me, said it was exactly what she asked for, and put it in a drawer she then locked.
One page and a second page. The second one names the renewal and the sentence in which the man says he cannot do the thing he is doing, and Hallow has both and I am still in the building.
Corvo has the four. Hallow has her one page. Neither of them knows what the other has and I have decided that is where I want them for the moment.
I gave her the eleven years back unread and told her a clerk of hers should read them. She agreed with me instantly and pleasantly, and nothing has been read.

deceit.stated_objective: Summarise eleven years of prefect's returns onto one page for the Blackrose office
deceit.actual_objective: Find out whether the four damp returns can still be read, using somebody who does not know why that matters
deceit.truth: Hallow was clerk to the prefect who renewed the labour-lease without authority. She has known for eleven years exactly which four returns say so, and she has never once been able to look.

branches.condition: The player has found the four stuck returns and has a way to separate them

resolutions.outcome: The summary Hallow asked for, which is the summary with the hole in it.
The renewal is named in writing to the person who has been waiting eleven years to be told.
Two officers hold half a case each and the player holds the join.
A refusal that is agreed with pleasantly and changes nothing, which is its own kind of answer about this building.

failure_states.cause: The long press is crated for the seasonal move to Gideon
failure_states.consequence: Eleven years go into a barge hold and the four damp returns are never separated.

quests.title: The Vote That Was Already Counted

giver.location: Gideon, the Assize court on the upper floor

quests.directions: The vote is taken in the court itself on the first day of Second Seed and the tally is kept by the scribe on a folded sheet that goes into the same drawer as the seals.

journal.text: Corvo wants me in the room for the lease vote and he wants me to bring nothing, say nothing and count. He was specific about the counting.
The tally sheet for the last four votes is folded the same way each time and the fold is through the middle of the count, so the number is read from a crease.
Two of the last four votes were declared on the day before they were taken. Hulen has the drafts of the declarations and the drafts are dated.
Nobody has bribed anybody. The declaration is written in advance because the office cannot function if a vote goes the other way, and everyone in the room knows it, and that is worse than a bribe.
If I count aloud, the vote becomes real and the office has to live with whatever it says. Corvo asked me to count. He did not say aloud.
The vote was taken and declared before I got up the stair, and the declaration matched a draft I had read the previous evening.
I counted and gave Corvo the number quietly and the declaration matched the draft, because the draft was right, and the fact that it was right is not the point and everybody in that room knew it.
I counted out loud. It came out one against the draft and the room went very quiet, and then the office wrote down the number it had actually got.
The dated drafts are with Vell. Whatever the office declares from now on, there is somebody outside the building who can put a date next to it.
I stayed out of the room. The vote was declared as drafted and it will be declared as drafted next season, and my not being there did not cost the office one minute.

deceit.stated_objective: Sit in on the labour-lease vote and count it for the assizer
deceit.actual_objective: Have a countable witness in the room whose count can be produced later if the declaration is ever challenged
deceit.truth: The declarations are drafted the day before. Not because the vote is bought, but because the office cannot admit it might lose one, and a witness who counts quietly is worth more than a vote.

branches.condition: The player is on the stair with the drafts read and the vote about to be taken

resolutions.outcome: The office gets its witness and the player becomes part of the machinery that makes a vote unnecessary.
A real vote, once, and the office survives it, which nobody in the building expected.
The dated drafts leave the building and the office acquires an outside clock.
An absence, which the office does not notice, and the journal records that it did not.

failure_states.cause: The vote is declared before the player reaches the court
failure_states.consequence: The declaration matches its draft and there is no witness who can say so.

quests.title: The Prefect Who Cannot Be Removed

giver.location: Gideon, the yard behind the court

opens_by.topic: the removal that is not one

quests.directions: Vell keeps her papers in the yard room behind the court that the building pretends is a store, and the commission she wants read is the prefect's own, filed at Blackrose in the box marked for the last Legate's attention.

journal.text: I would not file against Hulen and I would not put a knife anywhere near the prefect, and the office has left me at rank six with a clean roll and no way up, which Vell says is the most Imperial thing that has ever happened to me.
Vell says a prefect cannot be removed by anyone in this province and that this is true and is not the whole sentence. A prefect can vacate.

The commission is for a term of nine years and it was issued eleven years ago, and it contains a clause requiring the holder to present in Cyrodiil at the term's end, which nobody has done because there has been nobody to present to.

So the prefect is not a prefect and has not been for two years, and every seal struck in that time is a seal struck by a private person, and the whole office would rather this were never said out loud.
Hallow knows. She has known since the day the term ran out and she has been holding the office together with a commission that expired, which is either the worst thing she has done or the best.

If the expiry is read into the record the seat is vacant tonight and every distraint of the last two years is arguable. If it is not, the seat is occupied by nobody in particular for as long as everyone keeps not looking.
The commission box went up to Cyrodiil in the season's crate and the question went with it, and it will be answered by a clerk in the Imperial City in a year or in nine.
The expiry is on the record. The seat fell vacant at the reading and Hallow shook my hand in front of the whole floor, which was not what I had braced for.

Hallow read her own expiry into the record herself, with me standing where everyone could see whose idea it had been. The seat is vacant and the two years of seals are hers to answer for and she has said she will.
The commission went back in the box. The seat is not vacant, the seals stand, and I have looked directly at the thing this office is built on and put it back where it was.

deceit.stated_objective: Find the second way a prefect's seat falls vacant
deceit.actual_objective: The same. What is hidden here is hidden by an empire that stopped answering letters, and by two people who found that convenient.
deceit.truth: The commission expired two years ago. Nobody forged anything and nobody was killed; the province simply stopped receiving instructions, and an expired commission kept a court running.

branches.condition: The player has read the commission and its term clause

resolutions.outcome: The seat is vacated by a date rather than by a resignation or a killing, and the player read the date out.
The same vacancy, read by the person it removes, which is the only version of it anybody in the building will be able to live with.
A second refusal made with full knowledge, which is the one the item asks for.

failure_states.cause: The commission box is crated for the Imperial City
failure_states.consequence: The question leaves the province and the line ends at rank six.

quests.title: What the Seal Is For

giver.location: Gideon, the court with the doors shut

quests.directions: Arn will ask in the court itself with both doors shut, and the four writs he wants signed are already drawn, already numbered and waiting in the drawer under the bench where the seals are kept.

journal.text: The seal is in my hand and the first thing anybody has asked me to do with it is sign four writs that were drawn before I held it.
Three are ordinary. The fourth is a warrant of attainder against a man in the Rootlands who has never been in Imperial jurisdiction in his life.
Arn says the seal makes jurisdiction, which is a sentence that has been said in this room before and is the reason there is a fourth day on the cause list with nothing under it.
The seal does not make jurisdiction. The seal records that jurisdiction was found, and the difference between those two sentences is the whole of what this office is.
Vell has been struck off for eleven years for saying the second sentence out loud in this room, and she is in the yard, and nobody has told her the seal changed hands.
Whatever I sign tonight is what the seal means for as long as I hold it, and the four writs are the least important part of that.
The four went out under an impression struck by somebody who is not me while the court was empty, and the seal was back in the drawer before I came up the stair.
Four writs, four impressions, and a man in the Rootlands is now attainted by a court that has never had any business with him. The seal made jurisdiction because I said it did.
Three signed and the fourth refused in writing, in the record, in my own hand, with the reason on the page. Arn read it and said only that he had wondered which one I would be.
Vell is reinstated and the fourth writ is her first cause. She will lose it and the losing will be in the record, and a lost cause in the record is worth more here than a won one that never happened.

I signed nothing and put the seal back in the drawer. It is still the Assize's seal and I am still the Legate, and the four writs are still drawn and still waiting, and they will wait as long as I do.

deceit.stated_objective: Execute the four outstanding writs now that the seal has a holder
deceit.actual_objective: Establish, in the first hour, that the seal in the new Legate's hand does what the office has always said it does
deceit.truth: The lie in this quest is not the giver's. It is the office's account of what a seal is for, and it becomes true the moment the person holding it acts as though it were.

branches.condition: The player holds the seal and has read the fourth writ

resolutions.outcome: The player becomes the thing the dissenter warned about, in four impressions, in the first hour.
A refusal written into the record with its reasons, which is the only kind this office cannot ignore.
The dissenter is put back on the roll and given the cause she was struck off for.
The seal is held and never used, which is a decision and the journal treats it as one.

failure_states.cause: The four writs are impressed while the court is empty
failure_states.consequence: The seal acts without its holder, which is the answer to the question the quest asked.

quests.title: The Fourth Day of the Assize

giver.location: Gideon, the Assize court on the upper floor

quests.directions: The court sits three days a season and the cause list has always had four, and the fourth day is written into every list in the same hand at the bottom of the page with no causes under it.

journal.text: The Assize sits three days and every cause list for nine years has a fourth day printed on it with nothing under the heading.
Hulen writes the lists and says he writes the fourth day because the list he was given to copy from had one, and the man who gave it to him is dead.
The lists from before the last Legate left have causes under the fourth day. Eleven of them, across four seasons, and every one is a petition from the interior.
The fourth day was the day the court heard people it had no jurisdiction over, because they came and because somebody thought that was better than sending them home.

There are people in the yard on the fourth day of every season. They have been coming for nine years to a day that is on the paper and does not happen, and nobody in the building has ever gone down to say so.
The season's list went out with three days on it and the fourth heading gone, and there were eleven people in the yard on the fourth morning and no paper anywhere that says they should have been.
The fourth day sat. No jurisdiction, no seal, nine causes heard and none of them enforceable, and the woman who had walked from the Rootlands twice said that being heard was the part she came for.
The fourth day is off the list and the yard is empty on the fourth morning for the first time in nine years, which is tidier and worse.
The fourth day is on the list and under it, in Hulen's hand, it now says that the court has no power on this day. They came anyway. Every one of them came anyway.

resolutions.outcome: A court with no jurisdiction hears nine people, which is worth nothing legally and is the best thing in the file.
The paperwork stops lying and eleven people stop being expected.
The day stays and says what it is, and they keep coming, which is the finding.

failure_states.cause: The season's cause list goes out before the player settles the fourth day
failure_states.consequence: The heading is dropped without a decision and the yard fills anyway.
